questions.question: What is the space complexity of naive recursive Fibonacci, `fib(n) = fib(n - 1) + fib(n - 2)`?
options: O(2ⁿ), the same as its time
O(n), because the stack only holds one root-to-leaf path at a time
questions.explanation: Although there are exponentially many calls in total, at most n frames are on the stack at once, so stack space is O(n).

questions.question: Why is `const half = power(x, Math.floor(n / 2))` followed by `half * half` important in fast exponentiation?
options: Computing the half once keeps it to one recursive call per level, giving O(log n) instead of O(n)
It is required for negative exponents
questions.explanation: Calling power(x, n/2) twice per level doubles the calls at every level, which cancels the halving and makes the total O(n).

questions.question: Why does `sum(arr.slice(1))` make a recursive array sum slower than passing an index?
options: slice is not allowed in recursion
slice copies the array at every level, making the total time O(n²)
questions.explanation: Each slice costs O(n), done n times. Passing an index keeps each call O(1) and the total O(n).

questions.question: How many moves does the Tower of Hanoi solution make for 10 discs?
questions.explanation: The solution makes 2ⁿ - 1 moves, so for n = 10 that is 1023.
